defects.title: POST /canon/compute answers an unexpected exception with a plain-text 500 instead of the error envelope
defects.observed: With the kernel facade raising RuntimeError('boom /private/var/x'), the real FastAPI app answers `500`, `content-type: text/plain; charset=utf-8`, body `Internal Server Error` (not JSON). Controls on the same client: unknown fleet aircraft -> 404 `{"error":{"code":"not_found",...}}`; invalid body -> 422 `{"error":{"code":"validation_error",...}}`. The exception text does NOT leak (the body is the fixed Starlette string).
defects.expected: 500 with the one envelope `{"error": {"code": "internal_error", "message": ..., "details": ...}}`, without the exception text.
defects.requirement_source: _reversa_sdd/adrs/0019-implementation-details-must-not-leak-into-the-api.md, section Decision, item 3: 'Which internal code path produced a response - one error envelope ({"error": {code, message, details}}), one response contract per endpoint, regardless of which layer raised.' The ADR governs new surface; /canon/compute (gh-1282) is newer than the ADR (2026-08-14).
defects.root_cause: app/main.py:279-341 — exception handlers are registered only for ServiceException (279), IntegrityError (315) and RequestValidationError (330); any other exception falls through to Starlette's ServerErrorMiddleware, which answers in plain text. app/services/canon_service.py:223 lets a non-ServiceException from the kernel propagate unchanged.
defects.user_impact: The Expert View frontend (and any API client) gets a non-JSON 500 on an unexpected kernel/service failure and cannot show a structured error.
defects.note: Not specific to the canon endpoint: app/main.py has no catch-all handler, so every route of the app behaves this way; the ticket should say app-wide. No existing fast test has to change if the fix is a catch-all handler in app/main.py (app/tests/test_canon_service.py::test_a_failure_on_the_kernel_loop_reaches_the_caller pins the propagation inside the service and would have to change only if the fix were made in canon_service instead). Reachability: the kernel's own contract is 'a node never raises' (engine.py:395), so the trigger is a kernel or service defect, not ordinary input; reproduced with a raising stub only. Separate observation, not part of this finding: the default HTTPException handler still answers `{"detail": ...}`, a second envelope.

defects.title: endurance-and-range-optimum never returns for a stall speed of exactly 0 (scan loop cannot advance, time budget cannot interrupt it)
defects.observed: Formula called directly with the fast tests' doubles (SpeedOpti(min_speed=1.0), no real solver). v_s = 0.0: did not return, killed by the 20 s hard timeout; after 5 s the process is still in _Domain.scan with v = 0.0, ~9000 identical scan speeds [0.0, 0.0, ...] appended to the grid, 1 solver call, 0 speeds inside the domain; an asyncio.timeout(2 s) around the call never fired. Control v_s = 6.0 returns in 0.05 s. v_s = -3.0 does NOT hang with the stub: 7437 solver calls down to -inf, then an undeclared ValueError ('FormulaError detail.v_ms must be finite') after ~3 s. v_s = NaN: undeclared ValueError at once ('detail.stall_speed_ms must be finite'), raised while building the declared no_level_flight_speed error. Reachability: compute() with values['stall-speed'] = 0.0 is refused as invalid_input/not_an_input (stall-speed has role output).
defects.expected: A declared failure (precondition violated, or FormulaError no_level_flight_speed) for a stall speed that is not positive and finite, as the six powered-performance entries give through `stall_speed_usable`.
defects.requirement_source: (1) aero_kernel/formulas/endurance_and_range_optimum.py:128-133, docstring of _Domain.scan: 'Raises: FormulaError: no_level_flight_speed if no scan speed is inside the domain' - violated: no speed is inside, nothing is raised. (2) Same file, module docstring lines 9-21, 'The domain and its search (declared, never silent)'. (3) aero_kernel/ARCHITECTURE.md ch. 8.1 error table, row `timeout` ('the time budget was exceeded'), enforced by asyncio.timeout at aero_kernel/engine.py:1558 - a loop that never suspends cannot be cancelled by it. NO written requirement says that this canon entry must carry the precondition `stall_speed_usable`: _reversa_sdd/calculations/canon/formulas/endurance-and-range-optimum.md has no `preconditions:`; the gh-1419 remark that introduces the precondition (formulas/max-level-speed.md line 70) names the six powered entries only. Whether to add the precondition or a guard in the scan is a canon decision.
defects.root_cause: aero_kernel/formulas/endurance_and_range_optimum.py:134-140 — the scan advances by `v *= self._ratio`, which leaves v at 0 (and drives a negative v to -inf); `while v <= self.v_cap` then stays true, and because `at(v)` (lines 101-105) answers the repeated v = 0 from its cache the loop never awaits anything real, so it neither ends nor yields to the event loop.
defects.user_impact: None reachable through the public API today as far as reading shows (latent): if a stall speed of 0 ever reached this formula, the whole compute call - and the kernel event loop the app shares - would block for ever instead of timing out.
defects.note: LATENT, low priority: the trigger needs v_s == 0 exactly. Through compute() a caller cannot supply stall-speed (verified: not_an_input), and by reading its only producer (stall-speed formula, aero_kernel/solvers/opti.py:709, optimum inside a speed bracket; error-level postcondition cl_max_at_stall_reynolds_number divides by v_s) does not return 0 for validated input (mass > 0). The reviewer's claim '0 (or negative) never leaves the loop' is only half right: negative and NaN end in an undeclared ValueError (would be `internal` through the engine), not in a hang - with the stub; with the real solver each of the ~7400 negative speeds would cost a solve, but those awaits yield, so the time budget would end it. Real-solver behaviour at v = 0 not run (would need AeroBuildup): the hang needs the level-flight solve at v = 0 to fail with one of the four _EXIT_BOUNDS codes (e.g. not_converged), which the stub does and which is plausible but unverified for the real adapter; any other exception there would surface as `internal` instead. If the fix is a canon precondition: canon_model.json, the navigator and IMPORT_REPORT are regenerated, no existing fast test asserts the entry has no preconditions; a new test mirrors aero_kernel/tests/test_powered_scan_start.py::test_a_stall_speed_that_is_not_positive_finite_and_inside_the_scan_violates_it.

defects.title: Requesting lift-coefficient at flight speed 0 returns an `internal` error (ZeroDivisionError) instead of a declared one
defects.observed: evaluate() as in the fast test (stub atmosphere, mass 1.5 kg, altitude 0): flight-speed 10 -> dynamic-pressure ok 61.25 Pa, lift-coefficient ok. flight-speed 0.0 -> no input_errors, dynamic-pressure status ok value 0.0, lift-coefficient status error: category=internal, code=internal, escalate=True, message 'Internal error (ZeroDivisionError) while computing `lift-coefficient`.', hint 'Report it; attach input and provenance.'
defects.expected: A declared, non-escalating error that names the cause (e.g. precondition_violated on a positive dynamic pressure / flight speed), never `internal`.
defects.requirement_source: aero_kernel/ARCHITECTURE.md ch. 8.1, error-category table (lines 220-229): `internal` = 'programming error', escalate = yes, hint 'Report it'; an inadmissible input is `invalid_input`. Ch. 8.12 'Failure' (lines 1702-1708): 'Raise FormulaError(...) for an expected failure ... Any other exception becomes internal.' A value the caller may legally supply (flight-speed carries no `positive: true` in _reversa_sdd/calculations/canon/quantities/flight-speed.md, and V = 0 is a used operating point: static thrust) is an expected case. Precedent for the declared form: _reversa_sdd/calculations/canon/formulas/spanwise-loads.md line 30 and remark line 143 (#1398), precondition `flight_speed_positive` ('the operating point must give a dynamic pressure ... a violation is an error'). The canon entry formulas/lift-coefficient-required.md itself states no precondition - which one to add (on q or on V) is the canon's decision.
defects.root_cause: aero_kernel/formulas/lift_coefficient_required.py:26 — divides by `q * s_ref` with no guard, and the canon entry lift-coefficient-required declares no precondition, so q = 0 from the admissible flight-speed 0 raises ZeroDivisionError, which the engine translates to `internal` (engine.py:395).
defects.user_impact: An Expert View user or API client who evaluates the lift coefficient at V = 0 is told to report an internal kernel error, although the cause is their operating point.
defects.note: No existing fast test has to change if the fix is a precondition on lift-coefficient-required. Do NOT fix it by making flight-speed `positive: true`: V = 0 is used on purpose by aero_kernel/tests/test_powertrain_chain.py (builder line 90; test_q30_at_zero_speed_the_thrust_node_equals_the_thrust_inside_the_static_ratio) and test_motor_propeller_part_load.py:255, which would then have to change. Not checked: other formulas that divide by q or V may have the same gap; this finding covers lift-coefficient-required only. A canon precondition means regenerating canon_model.json and the navigator.

defects.title: Canon importer does not scan taxonomy.yaml for `# ESCALATED:` comments and YAML 1.1 booleans (defaults.yaml, rules.yaml, config.yaml and all entries are scanned)
defects.observed: import_canon on a temporary copy of the real canon: unmodified -> 0 findings, model built. taxonomy.yaml with `modules:  # ESCALATED: undecided module list` -> 0 findings, model built. Control, same comment in defaults.yaml -> 1 finding ('defaults.yaml: ESCALATED: ...'), no model. taxonomy.yaml with `holds_targets: yes` -> 0 findings, model built, holds_targets read as True. Control, `zz-probe: yes` in rules.yaml -> finding 'rules.yaml: yaml: YAML 1.1 reads ['yes'] as booleans'.
defects.expected: If the rule is meant for the whole canon document: one finding per case and no model, as for the other three YAML files.
defects.requirement_source: No written requirement names taxonomy.yaml. What exists: aero_kernel/ARCHITECTURE.md ch. 8.9 lines 1188-1192 - 'The canon uses no key or value that YAML 1.1 reads as a boolean' (a statement about the canon, enforcement stated only as 'A boolean where the schema expects a string is a stage-1 finding') and 'An ENTRY that carries [an # ESCALATED: comment] is a stage-1 finding: the importer imports nothing until the maintainer has decided it'. Canon README 'Escalated fields' (lines 528-533) defines the comment for the front matter of an entry; README line 462 'Keys and values avoid YAML 1.1 booleans' stands under 'Machine-readable fields' of entries. The stage-1 module docstring (aero_kernel/importer/parse.py:1-8) lists 'every entry, defaults.yaml, rules.yaml and config.yaml' - not taxonomy.yaml. So the behaviour contradicts the general sentence about 'the canon' and is inconsistent with the three sibling files, but no text says taxonomy.yaml must be scanned.
defects.root_cause: aero_kernel/importer/parse.py:478-519 — `_read_taxonomy` is a separate reader that never calls `_scan_front_matter(text, file, findings)`, unlike `_read_slug_map` (line 460) and `_read_front` (line 232).
defects.user_impact: Only the canon author: an undecided marker or a `yes`/`no` in taxonomy.yaml passes `importer --check` unnoticed; no wrong number results (PyYAML reads `yes` as the same True that `true` gives).
defects.note: The task summary says 'not checked ... by scripts/check_canon.py' - that is imprecise: scripts/check_canon.py contains no ESCALATED or YAML-1.1 scan for ANY file (grep is empty; the structural rules moved to the importer, #1174). The finding is about the importer (production_ref parse.py:478), and that is what was reproduced. Scanning the shipped taxonomy.yaml and the test fixture MINI_TAXONOMY + FAMILIES with _scan_front_matter gives no finding, so no existing fast test and not the real canon would break if the scan were added. Practical harm today is small; recommend deciding it as a one-line consistency fix rather than filing it as a bug.

defects.title: Traceability check accepts a @relation registered for a formula slug the canon model does not have
defects.observed: Fresh Registry, shipped canon model: only `relation('no-such-formula')` registered -> registry.slugs() == [], check_traceability(model).ok is True, findings []; load_build(registry=...) returns a Build. Controls: `formula('no-such-formula')` or `precondition('no-such-formula', 'a')` -> ok False, finding ('unknown_formula', 'calc:no-such-formula'), and load_build raises CanonLoadError.
defects.expected: Finding `unknown_formula` for calc:no-such-formula; the Build does not load.
defects.requirement_source: aero_kernel/ARCHITECTURE.md ch. 8.12, bullet 'Traceability' (lines 1765-1770): 'Registry.check_traceability(model) ... reports a registered slug or check id the model does not have (unknown_formula, unknown_check)'. aero_kernel/registry.py:312-315, docstring of check_traceability: 'Reports a registered slug the model does not have'. aero_kernel/registry.py:259, docstring of slugs(): 'the qualified slugs of every formula with ANY registration' - the code leaves the relations out. Caveat: the same ARCHITECTURE bullet still ends with '`@relation` and the embedding checks arrive with the first embedded formula (ADR 0021)', a sentence that predates the five shipped @relation registrations; it shows the relation case was not thought through when the check was written, but it does not exempt relations.
defects.root_cause: aero_kernel/registry.py:260 — `slugs()` collects `self._implementations` and `self._checks` only, not `self._relations`, so check_traceability (line 324) never looks at a relation's slug.
defects.user_impact: Only kernel developers: a misspelt slug in @relation loads cleanly, the embedder is then silently handed no relation (engine.py:702-704 skips a missing one) and fails at run time instead of at load.
defects.note: All five shipped @relation slugs exist in the model, so the shipped build stays `ok` after a fix. No existing fast test has to change (aero_kernel/tests/test_relations.py never calls check_traceability; test_registry_check.py registers no relation). ARCHITECTURE ch. 8.12 should lose the stale 'arrive with the first embedded formula' sentence in the same change.
